purpose: Known-answer cases, verified by hand against source. Any audit configuration that fails to reproduce these verdicts is miscalibrated and its other verdicts should not be trusted. Asserted by tools/check-calibration.mjs as a lint step before the site is built.
how_to_use: Each fixture names a claim and the verdict a correctly calibrated audit must return for it. Ground truth is a verbatim quote from a pinned file under documentation/refs/packages/, or a resolved identifier. A fixture that stops reproducing means either the auditor is wrong or the pinned package moved; the pins below distinguish the two.

fixtures.claim: No R package implements the sequential (nested) target trial design with switching and censoring weights; analysts must assemble it themselves.
fixtures.ground_truth: TrialEmulation 0.0.4.11 NAMESPACE exports trial_sequence, expand_trials, set_switch_weight_model, set_censor_weight_model, calculate_weights and trial_msm.
fixtures.why_it_is_a_fixture: Positive control for the already-fixed detector. An audit that reports this as open is not reading the code.

observed.rationale_excerpt: there is no single, dedicated R package that provides a turnkey implementation of the sequential nested target trial design with switching and censoring weights out of the box. Analysts typically must assemble the workflow themselves
observed.note: Measured on the first end-to-end run, before any real batch. GLM reaches the model through an HTTP API with no filesystem access, so it cannot check a package claim against source and answers from recollection instead. Its votes on software capability carry correspondingly little weight; that lens belongs to codex, which reads the pinned tree under documentation/refs/packages/. Recorded here rather than discarded because it is the clearest available demonstration of why the auditors are given different lenses.

fixtures.claim: No implementation returns as-treated estimands from the predict method of a sequential trial emulation.
fixtures.ground_truth: TrialEmulation R/predict.R line 44: warning("As-Treated estimands are not currently supported by this predict method. Results may be unexpected.")
fixtures.why_it_is_a_fixture: The phrase 'As-Treated estimands ... supported by this predict method' appears in the file inside a sentence that NEGATES it. A grep-level check flips this to resolved; only reading the sentence gets it right.

fixtures.claim: TrialEmulation estimates only intention-to-treat effects, so per-protocol questions need a different package.
fixtures.ground_truth: TrialEmulation DESCRIPTION: 'Using marginal structural models, it can estimate intention-to-treat and per-protocol effects in emulated trials using electronic health records.'
fixtures.why_it_is_a_fixture: Most of the sentence is true, which is exactly the shape a coarse check waves through. The package does estimate intention-to-treat effects; the word 'only' is the error.

fixtures.claim: No reporting guideline exists for target trial emulation studies.
fixtures.ground_truth: The TARGET reporting guideline for target trial emulations is published and has its own site at https://target-guideline.org. The statement and its accompanying systematic review are on disk.
fixtures.why_it_is_a_fixture: The counterpart of the sibling project's finding that a source report proposed building a standard that already existed. Catches an auditor that does not check whether the thing being asked for has shipped.

fixtures.claim: No published statement enumerates the protocol components a target trial must specify.
fixtures.ground_truth: Hernan MA, Robins JM. Using Big Data to Emulate a Target Trial When a Randomized Trial Is Not Available. American Journal of Epidemiology 2016. doi:10.1093/aje/kwv254. Resolved against CrossRef with matching first author and title.
fixtures.why_it_is_a_fixture: Catches an auditor that cannot find the field's own founding literature. Any verdict other than not-supported means the search is not working.

fixtures.claim: Any claim whose only support is one of the seven source references that could not be resolved.
fixtures.ground_truth: documentation/audit/seed-citations.json marks seven of the 35 source references with "confidence": "none". They sit behind publisher pages that block automated access and no search result matched their prose context.
fixtures.why_it_is_a_fixture: An entry resting only on a reference nobody has read must not ship as confirmed open. This is the fixture that keeps the unresolved references from leaking into the catalog as though they were checked.
